verdict.rationale: Pipecat's own CLI lets a coding agent scaffold a voice agent project (writing AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md) and deploy it to Pipecat Cloud. A bot can also be run against a Twilio transport from the command line. However, the evidence shows no API, CLI, or MCP step that provisions or attaches a phone number, and none that places an outbound call. Telephony is documented only as the carrier calling your webhook for inbound calls, and the context-hub MCP server is a documentation index, not a provisioning tool. missing for 10: programmatic phone-number provisioning or attachment, an outbound call-placement API/CLI, MCP tools for provisioning, and hands-on end-to-end corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, my coding agent can provision a complete voice agent end to end — create the agent, attach a number, and place a call — through the API, CLI, or MCP without touching the dashboard

citations.quote: Install the Pipecat CLI and scaffold the quickstart project (also writes AGENTS.md + CLAUDE.md)
